# Change Dossier: Reclaimable Space As Whole Objects

- Dossier: `DOSSIER-PLAN-DISK-STEWARD-006-R10-G202`
- Plan: `PLAN-DISK-STEWARD-006`
- Completed at: `2026-10-04T22:39:56.955460Z`
- Completed by: `claude`
- Baseline: revision `4` → `5`

## Intent

Disk Steward treats build output, shared developer caches and repositories as single evidence objects rather than per-file rows, so a real-sized scope finishes scanning inside the configured limit and the user sees where reclaimable space actually is, with a stated rebuild path and an explicit review step before anything is removed.

## Inspections

- `INSPECT-RESEARCH-601-1` — Confirm the measurement tool only reads: no write, move or delete in a measured corpus and no project tooling executed; confirm the fixture self-test asserts the deciding rule for every case including the tracked refusal; confirm every claim in the note resolves to measurement.json or candidates.jsonl from the archived runs. (pass, sufficient)
- `INSPECT-CONTRACT-601-1` — Confirm every contract rule names the task that proves it and a check that can hold it; confirm the detection order and confidence vocabulary match the measured outcome of RESEARCH-601; confirm no rule weakens an inherited guarantee of the closed reliability plan. (pass, sufficient)
- `INSPECT-TASK-611-1` — Confirm the rule order matches CONTRACT-601 and RESEARCH-601; confirm tracked source is refused before any other rule and that an optional oracle answer cannot decide by accident; confirm classification performs no write and executes no project tooling; confirm each acceptance case has a test and that disabling a load-bearing rule fails it. (pass, sufficient)
- `INSPECT-TASK-613-1` — Confirm the object row carries the contract's fields and that review-required and the measurement-time rule are enforced by the schema, not by convention; confirm a collapse is transactional per object, bounded to its own subtree, closes bindings rather than deleting them, is idempotent and resumes after interruption; confirm the migration from the previous schema is rehearsed with a working rollback to the baseline binary. (pass, sufficient)
- `INSPECT-TASK-612-1` — Confirm a classified object is recorded and never entered, that an unresolved candidate and tracked source are still scanned, that scan work is independent of an object's contents, that a generation completes and publishes its objects with no per-file row inside one, and that the pre-object behaviour survives when no classifier is supplied. (pass, sufficient)
- `INSPECT-TASK-615-1` — Confirm the probe constructs its scanner with the classifier and the repository oracle; confirm an existing store converges in bounded batches, stops when nothing remains, and reports what it changed; confirm a probe without a classifier behaves exactly as before; confirm the ancestor walk is bounded and refuses non-absolute paths, with the diagnosed hang reproduced by a mutation. (pass, sufficient)
- `INSPECT-R3-616-CONTAINMENT` — Verify the task's complete owned-descendant bootstrap matrix, aggregate-memory metric, finite budgets, identity/PID reuse protections, retained-stdout/parent-exit/group-escape paths, unrelated-process sentinel and independent exit checks. Confirm all focused/mutation/candidate/package/rollback/soak entry points enforce the same safety contract or refuse launch. Only after small bounded fixtures pass, inspect a bounded real Swift/XCTest smoke report. (pass, sufficient)
- `INSPECT-R3-616-EVIDENCE` — Check reproducible commands, baseline/candidate hashes, stop reasons, metrics and zero-owned-survivor evidence. Verify no unsafe bootstrap or production-state access and that documentation no longer equates top-level timeout with cleanup. (pass, sufficient)
- `INSPECT-R3-617-PRESENTATION` — Exercise successive hosted-view updates with fake lifecycle/notification fixtures: +5.6 GB alert then +2.1 MB then decrease, real bounded single-flight refresh, pause/restart/error/reopen and separate capacity/detail freshness. Compare visibly rendered state and event IDs/intervals; do not accept model-only getters. (pass, sufficient)
- `INSPECT-R3-617-MEASUREMENT` — Verify signed per-volume delta/baseline selection and ordinary/refusal paths with synthetic samples, matching alert/presentation intervals, bounded one-record session lifetime, no live files/notifications and no schema migration. Confirm TASK-616 resource and cleanup receipts accompany all runs. (pass, sufficient)
- `INSPECT-R3-623-INTEGRATION` — Verify object presentation and read-only API contract without regressing TASK-617's rendered sequential updates, separate freshness or bounded latest alert. Retain existing response limits, privacy and repository non-candidate behavior. (pass, sufficient)

## Findings and Residual Risk

- `FIND-R3-ORPHANED-TEST` — TASK-616: verifier timeout left an orphaned XCTest with 86.9G footprint; descendant containment must be proven before further candidate runs (critical, resolved)
- `FIND-R3-DASHBOARD` — TASK-617: reported frozen dashboard, cached refresh, discarded decreases and missing alert interval context need rendered regression proof (high, resolved)
- `FIND-R4-IDLE-CPU` — GATE-649: installed 1.3.0 (9) averaged 11.4% of a core after the stop; event-triggered samples recomputed lifecycle status (high, resolved)
- `FIND-R4-XCODE-WORKER` — xcodebuild leaves one worker after a successful packaged or archive build; supervision stops it and verifies cleanup, and stages record launcher-exited-with-descendants (medium, accepted)
- `FIND-R4-SUPERVISOR-RACE` — process_supervisor fails closed with 'Cannot classify new process' several times an hour before any test runs; runs are retried, never relabeled (medium, resolved)
- `FIND-R4-OBJECT-CONVERGENCE-FLAKE` — ObjectConvergenceTests seed step intermittently throws 'change evidence is later than observation publication', also on unmodified main (low, accepted)
- `FIND-R4-LIFECYCLE-RESPONSE-SIZE` — get_evidence_lifecycle returns ~58 KB on the live store, too large for an agent context; rung 4 replaces it with get_health (low, resolved)
- `FIND-R4-PAGE-SCHEMA-STALE` — Schemas/MCP/evidence-query-page-v1.schema.json is unenforced and stale: explain_growth's surviving_* keys (pre-existing) and TASK-652's detail_status, capacity_change, changed_directories, journal_* and coverage 'unavailable' are not listed; rework with the rung-4 tool contract (low, accepted)
- `FIND-R4-PATH-REDACTION-FALSE-POSITIVE` — The MCP path privacy filter redacts 'sk-…' inside ordinary names ('.disk-steward-gate-659' became '.di[REDACTED]'); it hides rather than leaks; pre-existing (low, accepted)
- `FIND-R4-JOURNAL-LIMIT` — explain_growth's changed_directories ignores the request limit and uses a fixed 200-item window (still bounded by the response ceiling) (low, accepted)
- `FIND-R4-DOCS-STALE` — docs/architecture/mcp.md and docs/operations/privacy-and-retention.md still describe the retired file-level tools and the old store's time/byte retention at tag v1.4.0 (left unchanged to keep the verified input hash); update with the rung-3/4 tool rework (low, resolved)
- One corpus on one machine; the share that git can decide will differ elsewhere.
- 27 candidates stay unresolved by design and need an explicit user override rather than a guess.
- Sizes are logical lstat bytes, not allocated blocks.
- The contract is a specification, not evidence; each rule stays unproven until its named task passes its gate.
- Sizes are logical bytes and will read slightly under what the volume reports; every surface must say so.
- The 27 unresolved candidates need an explicit override path; the contract forbids guessing but does not yet specify the override.
- GitRepositoryOracle is compiled but not exercised against a real repository by these tests; TASK-612 wires and exercises it.
- Content evidence reads one directory level, so an unusual layout falls through to a weaker rule rather than a wrong one.
- Nothing in the product calls the classifier yet, so no user-visible behaviour changed.
- Objects publish without aggregates until TASK-621; a reader must not read a missing size as zero.
- The app's monitoring probe does not construct the scanner with a classifier yet, so installed behaviour is unchanged.
- The scale fixture is uniform and synthetic; it proves cost independence, not the variety of a real disk.
- Volume enumeration costs ~0.4 s per sample on this Mac; bounded by the 5-minute interval while stopped, replaced in rung 2.
- Supervisor 'Cannot classify new process' failures are now frequent (several per hour).
- Cold-cache timing needs sudo purge; both recorded runs are warm.
- No product surface starts a review yet (TASK-623 window, TASK-671 agents).
- Many concurrent git children trip the supervisor's classification race; the oracle keeps at most four open.
- Not hostile-code or launchd/XPC containment
- Sampled stop thresholds can overshoot
- PID signal checks are not an atomic kernel birth-ID kill
- Legacy scale/soak/corpus/rollback entry points refuse execution rather than claim a passing rerun
- Installed app and live evidence unchanged; no package/notarization/release or large-scope gate is claimed.
- File attribution can cover a different interval than capacity; notifications explicitly qualify it.
- UUID-unavailable filesystems cannot establish a comparable growth baseline.
- Other plan-006 object/scope tasks and increment gates remain unfinished.
- Non-summary tools still read coverage gaps unbounded for their verdicts; TASK-671 replaces them.
- Backend construction on a locked store still waits on SQLite locks (pre-existing).
- Other detail tools return a retryable deadline error on a locked store.

- The design document's data-model table is stale; corrected separately outside this task's assets.
- Hosted rendering of the new reserve line is covered through the view model, not a screenshot.
- AppEvidenceQueryBackend's ring read (TASK-651, already audited) no longer creates capacity.sqlite; get_storage_summary reports an empty history instead when the ring file is absent.
- Schemas/MCP/evidence-query-page-v1.schema.json is not enforced and was already stale (explain_growth's surviving_* keys); it does not list detail_status, capacity_change, changed_directories, journal_* or coverage 'unavailable'.
- Gap flags other than a journal-identity change cannot be induced on real FSEvents; their mapping is tested with synthetic records.
- TCC: delivery without Full Disk Access is observed; dependence on per-folder consent is confirmed with the installed app at GATE-659.
- Two settings emissions in quick succession start two restarts; the last stream start wins, so no stream leaks, but self.roots may briefly lag.
- MCP export_evidence cannot inline a store with ~100k current files (2 MiB budget); legacy exports now say so and point to the file export. Pre-existing on 1.3.0 as a retryable request_too_large.
- Agent sessions are in memory until rung 4 persists them in the steward file; a relaunch requires re-registration through Scripts/Integration/session.
- The retired scanner, retention and convergence code remains (unreachable) for its rung-1 tests until rung 3 removes it.
- Installing 1.3.0 without first running restore-legacy-evidence would start an empty store and resume scanning; the script must run first.
- The supervisor's process-classification race (FIND-R4-SUPERVISOR-RACE) stopped a full-suite run and one mutation run; both were rerun.
- The path privacy filter redacts sk-… inside ordinary path names (FIND-R4-PATH-REDACTION-FALSE-POSITIVE).
- A clean 1.3.0 quit leaves an uncheckpointed WAL; the legacy move carries it, and any rollback must restore it too (the script does).
- The candidate is not notarized (the user's choice); Gatekeeper acceptance is unproven for 1.5.0.
- FIND-R4-OBJECT-CONVERGENCE-FLAKE recurs in full runs (retired scanner path).
- This Claude session's own MCP connection still runs the 1.4.0 helper started before the install; a client restart picks up the new catalogue.
- The collapse acts on the objects it is given; classifying a real store's directories to choose them is TASK-612.
- Nothing measures a subtree yet, so most rows carry zero bytes and no measured_at until TASK-621.
- The rehearsal uses a synthetic store written by the baseline library rather than a copy of an installed one; a capture of a live store would have required opening it.
- Convergence is exercised against stores built in the test, not a copy of this machine's installed store; that capture belongs to the rung gate.
- Objects still publish without aggregates until TASK-621.
- A directory that no longer exists classifies as unresolved, so its rows wait for an ordinary scan to remove them.
- FIND-R4-OBJECT-CONVERGENCE-FLAKE recurred (3 of the last 9 full runs); it lives in the retired scanner path.
